about: Cub Scouting is a family program for kids in kindergarten through 5th grade. Scouts learn by doing: hands-on activities, outdoor adventures, and service projects, working through age-appropriate adventures with their families.
Scouts live by the Scout Oath and Scout Law and the Cub Scout motto, "Do Your Best." Adult leaders and parents guide, encourage, and support every Scout's journey.

groups_intro: One den per grade. Dens meet on their own, and the whole pack gathers for the pack meeting.

join_steps.title: Contact Us
join_steps.text: Email us with your Scout's name, grade, and school. We'll answer any questions.

join_steps.title: Visit a Meeting
join_steps.text: Come to a meeting and see what we're about.

join_steps.title: Apply Online

uniform: Scouts wear the Cub Scout uniform for meetings and ceremonies, plus the handbook for their rank. Both are available from the Scout Shop. Ask us about used uniforms.

safety.title: Youth Protection
points: Every adult leader completes Scouting America's Safeguarding Youth training and a background check.
Two registered adults are present at every activity. No one-on-one contact between adults and youth.
We post photos of Scouts only with written permission from a parent or guardian, and never with a Scout's full name.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
Can we visit before we join?
faq.a: Yes! Come to any meeting. Email {email} first so we can watch for you.

faq.q: Which den will my Scout be in?
faq.a: One den per grade: Lion (K), Tiger (1st), Wolf (2nd), Bear (3rd), Webelos (4th), and Arrow of Light (5th).
Yes. Cub Scouting is a family program, and adults stay on site during meetings. Lions and Tigers take part with an adult partner.
A uniform and the handbook for their rank, both available from the Scout Shop. Ask us about used uniforms.
